text: But: who are people using this products? Appliance poor adjustable characteristics explain the reason of an unilateral comprehension effort: from person to machine. text: Rather than green, we will speak about [...] environmentally preferable products, or "preferable" to others in the same conditions. [...] a product, a method, a system cannot be considered as absolute because this ecological absolute quality is deeply variable. It's better to talk about preferability, a term that relates that at that time, in those specific conditions, both for the environmental and the economic points of view, that particular product or service is better than another. [2: 43, translation mine]

text: Green Kitchen "diverts" 60% of the water and heat generated from appliances to fuel other functions and appliances. For example: the heat produced in the compressor coils from running the fridge (the one appliance that cycles on and off, 24 hours a day) is used to heat water for the dishwasher, rather than just wafting out into the kitchen.
source_title: Users and households appliances: design suggestions for a better, sustainable interaction

text: The concept of natural sound has been treated by Norman. He laments the massive presence of artificial sounds related to home appliances. Natural sounds are the ones related to the normal operation of the appliance (i.e. water noise in a dishwasher program communicates the process).
source_title: Users and households appliances: design suggestions for a better, sustainable interaction
